title: Equivalent bounded witnesses
statement: Let $R_1,R_2$ be predicates on natural numbers and let $a,K\in\mathbb{N}$. If it is not the case that both $R_1(a)$ and $R_2(a)$ hold, then there exists an $m$ with $a+1\leq m<K$ satisfying both predicates if and only if there exists an $m$ with $a\leq m<K$ satisfying both predicates.
hypotheses_covered: It is not the case that both $R_1(a)$ and $R_2(a)$ hold
